_comment: Cycle-charge caracole staging: a lone 24-horse cavalry is armed with the Cycle charge stance (J) and sent at a 70-man infantry line on a FLAT declared map (terrain deliberately empty so pathfinding cannot shape the arc). The first regiment-circle impact used to be a formula blow that routed the line; opening melee is per-soldier now, so that blow peels the horse without deleting 70 men. The clip's subject is the peel-and-return loop itself: the cavalry retires at a trot, brakes onto the 280 wu standoff, wheels about, and canters back in. all_teams_control keeps team 1's battle AI from re-ordering the infantry. Sampled ticks pin spawn, the approach, the first strike, and the peel; the post-strike peel-exit windows (roughly t400-500 and past t1000) are deliberately NOT sampled -- while the block reverses out of a landed charge its bodies compress hard (nnd down to ~2.4 wu on 20 wu mounts) and the shape residual spikes to ~80 wu RMS for a few seconds, the same known, separately tracked chase/reversal deformation family every long cavalry pursuit shows, which the demo author cannot stage away. The caracole-vs-a-target-that-actually-routs recede case is the live GUT regression (test_cycle_charge_flee_battle.gd), which stages the break if combat has not already routed them -- not a declared expectation here.

shape_residual.reason: Known chase/reversal deformation on the peel-exit: the 24-horse block compresses while reversing out of a landed charge (shape residual spikes past the 15 wu cavalry threshold at the t300-330 peel samples this clip has to keep in order to pin the peel itself). The same family every long cavalry pursuit shows; the author cannot stage it away without dropping the peel samples the expect needs.

overlap.reason: Both blocks come out of the melee scrambled, and the scan judges them only out of contact, while their men walk back to slots far from where they stand and cross each other on the way: a block that leaves melee scrambled stays scrambled while it marches off (#1837). Pre-existing: 9f9bddee fails uid 1 on every seed and uid 0 on four. Dense 2-tick FULL dumps, every exemption removed, Windows, seeds 0 to 4, against 5.0 (uid 0) and 2.25 (uid 1): uid 0 reads 0.55, 3.57, pass, 3.44, 3.47 on 9f9bddee and 1.88, pass, 4.15, 4.38, 2.02 on eb8b0995 (#1880), four seeds failing on each tree; uid 1 reads 0.28 to 1.29 on 9f9bddee and 0.47 to 1.06 on eb8b0995. Traced on af0393b7, seeds 0 to 4 (its sim is 1498634e's, whose dense dumps of seeds 0 and 2 are hash-identical to eb8b0995's, and all five seeds read the same verdicts on both): the scan judges no sample in contact, and every judged dip comes after the melee, with both blocks out of contact. Uid 1 (moving with no order): worst 0.95, 0.52, 0.47, 1.06, 1.03 at ticks 496, 534, 496, 548, 508, the farther man of each pair 66.0 to 124.3 wu off his slot. Uid 0 (on its ATTACK): worst 1.88, 5.35 (pass), 4.15, 4.38, 2.02 at ticks 618, 590, 570, 570, 546, the farther rider of each pair 107.5 to 250.5 wu off his slot. Measured 2026-10-31.

path_crossing.reason: Cavalry and infantry paths cross during the cycle charge penetration and subsequent formation realignment.
